item.title: What an Agent Really Is: DeepSeek Support Agent vs OpenManus vs Grok Bot, Explained as Teams of Bots
item.description: Skip the jargon: an agent is just a team of bots that talk to each other in the background, split up your request, and hand you the finished result. Here is how DeepSeek Support Agent, OpenManus, and Grok Bot differ in who does what, and how to pick.

item.title: How to Read a "284B on 64GB, No GPU" Headline
item.description: A reading method for hardware-optimization headlines: bit-width, prefill vs decode, KV budget, real quality — walked on the open-source llama-modchip.

item.title: ARTEX: The Championship Pentest Tool That Ended Up in the Korean Bank Breach List
item.description: ARTEX, champion of Baidu's agent+ challenge, was turned against nine Korean banks; the upstream repo is down and ThreatBook is commercializing it. Someone on linux.do got shells in two hours.

item.title: dsh's Composer Started Guessing What You'll Say: 512 Tokens Buys Your Opening Move
item.description: DeepSeek Harness's community plugins give the dsh composer a 'guess what you'll say' layer: after each agent turn, ghost text drafts your next prompt and Tab adopts it. Bounded 512-token LLM calls plus local zsh-style prefix completion, with redaction and no core changes.

item.title: Can Plugins Unload Without a Trace? A 92-Page Paper from Peking University × DeepSeek Turns Plug-and-Unplug into Math
item.description: arXiv 2608.25512 introduces the programming paradigm of spatiotemporal composability: revertible effects make plugin removal leave no trace, reactive coeffects deactivate dependents automatically, unified as the context paradigm and implemented in Cordis — validated in production by Koishi's 4000+ plugin ecosystem. This is a paid article; the first half is free to read.

item.title: Who Draws the Kill Line for AI Models? Stop Letting Benchmarks Replace Engineering Reality
item.description: From prompt caching and thinking tokens to long context and inference infrastructure, a practical look at the real cost and engineering strength of Chinese foundation models.

item.title: DeepSeek Is No Longer Cheap: When the Price Disruptor Starts Charging for Compute
item.description: DeepSeek's peak and off-peak API pricing is more than a routine adjustment. It exposes the tension between low-price positioning, user expectations, and the real cost of running large models.

item.title: DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 Released: 1M Context, Official Price Hike Warning
item.description: DeepSeek released deepseek-v4-pro (0813) on 2026-08-13: 1M context, 384K max output, $0.435/M input and $0.87/M output, with cache-hit input at just $0.003625/M. The official docs also warn that overall API pricing will rise significantly in the near future. Includes Claude Code / Codex setup and community benchmark roundup.

item.title: DeepSeek Drops a Bombshell: V3.2-Exp Sparse Attention Mechanism Debuts, API Prices Slashed in Half Again
item.description: DeepSeek-V3.2-Exp released with groundbreaking DSA sparse attention technology, 2-3x faster inference, 30-40% memory reduction, and API prices cut by over 50%
